comparisons.title: VLOOKUP vs INDEX/MATCH
comparisons.purpose: Both find a value in one range and return a related value from another range.
advantages_b: Works in any direction (left or right)
limitations_a: Column index breaks when columns move
limitations_b: Two nested functions and a steeper learning curve
Slightly harder to audit for new users
comparisons.when_to_use: Use VLOOKUP for quick simple tables; use INDEX/MATCH when columns may move or you must look left.

comparisons.title: COUNTIF vs COUNTIFS
comparisons.purpose: Both count cells that satisfy criteria.
advantages_a: One condition, very easy to learn
limitations_a: Complex counting needs helper columns or SUMPRODUCT
limitations_b: Overkill when a single condition is enough
comparisons.when_to_use: Start with COUNTIF, then move to COUNTIFS as soon as a second condition appears.

comparisons.title: SUMIF vs SUMIFS
limitations_b: The sum range comes first, which confuses learners
comparisons.when_to_use: Use SUMIF for a single filter and SUMIFS for multi-criteria reports.

comparisons.title: IF vs IFS
comparisons.purpose: Both return values based on conditions.
advantages_a: Handles nested logic and defaults easily
advantages_b: Conditions read top-to-bottom like a menu
limitations_a: Nested IFs become hard to read after three levels
limitations_b: No built-in default branch unless TRUE is added last
comparisons.when_to_use: Use IF for simple yes/no checks and IFS for grading scales and tiered rules.

comparisons.title: VLOOKUP vs XLOOKUP
comparisons.purpose: Both return a value matched on a lookup key.
limitations_a: Column index breaks when columns move
Requires FALSE for exact match or errors appear
comparisons.when_to_use: Use XLOOKUP if you have Microsoft 365; keep VLOOKUP for older versions.

comparisons.title: CONCAT vs TEXTJOIN
comparisons.purpose: Both join text into a single string.
advantages_a: Fast for a handful of cells
advantages_b: Accepts a whole range in one argument
limitations_a: No separator control, commas must be added manually
comparisons.when_to_use: Use TEXTJOIN for lists and CONCAT for simple joins in older files.

comparisons.title: FIND vs SEARCH
comparisons.purpose: Both return the position of text inside a string.
limitations_a: Fails when the user types a different case
limitations_b: Wildcards may match more than expected
comparisons.when_to_use: Use FIND for strict parsing and SEARCH for casual keyword checks.
